findings.title: Outward release participates in protective positioning
findings.claim: The focus pair presents giving as an outward release that participates in placing a protective boundary around the person and the direction of the act.
findings.mechanism: The B002 giving carrier meets the focus self-guarding predicate, while the wider protective-garment image in 7:26 supplies a concrete barrier schema; their contact turns the coordinated predicates into one release-and-protection movement.
findings.reader_payoff: Giving becomes an operative relation within protection, so the two predicates read as connected acts rather than two adjacent character labels.
findings.containment: The primary remains whoever gives and guards themselves. This does not claim that giving alone causes safety or replace the ordinary sense of transfer with a barrier gloss.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run record is trusted and focus-anchored, while the participation arrow and the barrier image remain interpretive relations rather than grammatical assertions.
